texts.facts: The writ petition has been filed for issuance of Writ of Certiorarified Mandamus to quash the impugned order dated 06.11.2024 issued by the third respondent, and for a direction to respondents 1 to 3 to take action against the fifth respondent and his police force for their abusive and high-handed behavior towards rally participants on 07.11.2024, and for a direction to the respondents to compensate Rs.1.00 Crore for the financial losses incurred by the petitioners party, Puthiya Tamilagam, due to the unlawful denial of permission for the rally. 2. When the rally commenced at 9:00 AM on 07.11.2024, the police, acting under the orders of the fifth respondent, forcibly detained the participants in heavy rain, using excessive force. The denial of permission and the polices actions appear politically motivated and were designed to tarnish the image of the petitioners party. Hence, the petitioner made a representation to respondents 1 to 3 on 08.11.2024, requesting appropriate action against the fifth respondent for the atrocities committed against the participants and seeking compensation for the financial losses incurred. Therefore, the petitioner has filed the present writ petition. When the instructions were defied, the police took necessary action to prevent the illegal rally and arrested the participants. A case was registered for the offence under Section 189(2), 126(2), 132, 270 BNS r/w 41(6) of the Tamil Nadu City Police Act in Crime No. 489 of 2024 at F2 Dr.K.Krishnasamy vs The Secretary To Government on 6 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/141494349/ 3 Furthermore, while being transported in a government bus, the arrested individuals caused a ruckus, leading to the registration of a second case, Crime No.490 of 2024, for the offence under Sections 296(b) BNS and 3(1) of the PPDL Act.
texts.arguments: It is pertinent to point out that Article 19 of the Constitution of India guarantees certain fundamental freedoms, including the right to freedom of speech and expression and the right to assemble peacefully and without arms. This right is essential in a democracy as it allows citizens to express their views, hold peaceful protests, and come together for various causes, however, these rights are not absolute and can be restricted by the Government in certain situations to maintain public order, national security, and social harmony.
